title: Proper one-point bandits with smooth strongly convex losses on known convex bodies
summary: Expected static regret with exact bounded one-point feedback, feasible actions, and explicit domain conditioning and curvature budgets.

description_paragraphs: Minimize expected static regret for proper one-point adversarial bandit convex optimization on a known compact convex body, allowing boundary comparators.
task.formulation: Minimize expected static regret for proper one-point adversarial bandit convex optimization on a known compact convex body, allowing boundary comparators.

description_paragraphs: The public domain belongs to $\mathcal K_d=\{K:(4d)^{-1}B_2^d\subseteq K\subseteq B_2^d,\ K\text{ compact and convex}\}$. Every loss is the restriction of a continuously differentiable function on a neighborhood of $K$, takes values in $[0,1]$ on $K$, is $\mu$-strongly convex, and is $\beta$-smooth in the Euclidean norm on $K$. No globally bounded strongly convex extension is assumed.

An oblivious adversary fixes the loss sequence before the learner seed is drawn. The domain is known, the losses are hidden, and $0<\mu\le\beta$. Only domains with a nonempty loss class are included. The family is nonempty exactly when $\mu\le32d^2$.

The domain, horizon, and curvature budgets are public. Exact computations using the known domain are free; no additional loss information is included.

description_paragraphs: The executed actions must be feasible almost surely at every round. The static comparator is the minimizer of the cumulative loss over the same domain and can lie on its boundary.
output.feasibility: The executed actions must be feasible almost surely at every round. The static comparator is the minimizer of the cumulative loss over the same domain and can lie on its boundary.

description_paragraphs: $R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(X_t)-\min_{u\in K}\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(u)$. The minimax risk is $\mathfrak R^*_{T,\mathrm{sc}}(d;\mu,\beta)=\sup_{K\in\mathcal K_d:\mathcal F(K;\mu,\beta)\ne\varnothing}\inf_A\sup_{f_{1:T}}\mathbb E_A R_T$. The algorithm may depend on the known domain before the losses are selected.

description_paragraphs: All measurable randomized causal proper one-point policies are allowed. Computation on the known domain is unrestricted.
The guarantee is uniform over admissible oblivious loss sequences for each public domain; the risk subsequently takes the worst admissible domain.

regimes.predicate_text: $d,T\ge1$, $0<\mu\le\beta$, $\mu<32d^2$; choose $R_b\in[(4d)^{-1},1]$ with $M_b=\mu R_b^2<2$, $\Delta_b=1-M_b/2$, and $Q_b=\min\{M_b,\Delta_b^2/M_b\}$. Every finite d with an admissible witness radius. The lower bound holds for each admissible witness radius and hence for the worst-domain risk; it does not state a lower bound on every individual convex body.
